$comment: What lies between the two faces (docs/BIFACIAL_WORLD.md §2, §6; owner 2026-10-21: "add bedrock back in between the two faces … the portals are holes through the bedrock leading up to the surface on both sides"). `bedrock`: the block generated in the cells either side of the midplane, `thickness` metres on each face (a whole number of cells, inside the core). `portals`: a few vertical shafts per world, sited from the seed alone (crates/dwell-worldgen/src/portals.rs): `count` [min, max] of them (the seed picks the number), at least `spacing` m apart, within `within` m of the disc's centre, tried at up to `attempts` seeded points; a site needs dry land on both faces over its whole footprint (no river or lake), at least `inland` m from both coasts, its ground on both faces at most `maxHeight` m above sea level (the shaft is then at most 2 × (sea level + maxHeight) m long). The shaft is round, `radius` m (column centres within it are open from each face's ground to the midplane, the bedrock and core included); its opening is ringed `rim.width` m wide by `rim.height` m of `rim.block` over the ground; `ladder.block` runs the shaft's whole length on its `ladder.wall` side (north, east, south or west: the wall the ladder is fixed to), continuous across the midplane; no tree or decoration stands within `clear` m of the rim; `monument.structure` (shared/structures, or null for none) stands round every opening, its anchor on the shaft's axis and its bottom row on the lowest ground under its bottom layer (owner, 2026-10-26: pillars to make the portals easier to find), drawn in the LOD at levels whose cells are at most `monument.lodCellM` m (a cell holding any of its cells shows it, so it reads from afar); `motes` names the look of the glowing motes drawn in the shaft round the midplane (shared/look/motes.json; a client look, not terrain); `exit` is the push that carries a body swung up from the far face out of the opening onto the ground beside it (docs/BIFACIAL_WORLD.md §12.3; physics, not terrain): in a shaft's footprint, a body rising at least `exit.minRise` m/s with its feet within `exit.depth` m under the rim's top is pushed along its facing at `exit.push` m/s², a steady crosswind: however fast it rose, it lands about 2 × push × depth / gravity m out from where the push caught it (30 × 2: ~6 m from the axis, 2–4 m beyond the rim; a jump and a ladder climb are never pushed). Prototype content (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1). Changing any value but `motes` and `exit` changes the terrain a seed generates: regenerate the goldens (`cargo run -p dwell-worldgen --example goldens`) and ship it on a new compatibility line. Run `node shared/worldgen/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails on stale output.
